Two weeks before presentation, after backpacking travel to the northwestern United States, he developed cramping left calf pain that worsened over 2 days with swelling extending from the calf to the foot and a purpuric/erythematous rash on the dorsum of both feet. He also reported multiple prior self-limited similar respiratory episodes. On examination, he was uncomfortable from left leg pain, had left ankle synovitis, normal peripheral pulses, and an intact nasal septum.

Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (ANCA-a.description: A small- to medium-vessel necrotizing vasculitis that often affects the upper and lower respiratory tracts and kidneys, and can cause systemic inflammatory symptoms, skin lesions, and joint involvement.

IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein purpura.description: An immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis that typically causes palpable purpura, arthralgia/arthritis, abdominal pain, and sometimes renal involvement, often following an upper respiratory infection.

Septic thrombophlebitis / deep vein thro.normalized_text: Septic thrombophlebitis / deep vein thrombosis with overlying cellulitis or vasculitic-appearing rash
Septic thrombophlebitis / deep vein thro.description: A venous thrombosis, sometimes infected, causing painful swelling of a limb; can be accompanied by inflammatory skin changes and systemic symptoms if infection is present.

Leukocytoclastic vasculitis.description: A small-vessel cutaneous vasculitis that presents with palpable purpura, often on the lower extremities, and may be triggered by infection, medication, or systemic inflammatory disease.

Reactive arthritis.description: An inflammatory arthritis that follows an infection, commonly causing asymmetric lower-extremity arthritis and enthesitis; skin and mucosal findings can occur in some cases.

Crohn’s disease-associated extraintestin.description: Inflammatory bowel disease can rarely be associated with systemic or cutaneous vasculitic manifestations, including purpura, arthralgias, and inflammatory skin lesions.

case: A 47-year-old man presented to his primary care physician with a six-month history of left-sided sore throat, ipsilateral otalgia, and a six-week history of a left-sided neck mass. He had never smoked and drank less than 5 units of alcohol per week. On examination in the ENT clinic, a firm fixed lymph node was palpable in the upper anterior triangle.

Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.description: A malignant tumor arising from the lining of the tonsil, base of tongue, or other oropharyngeal sites; it commonly presents with persistent unilateral throat pain, referred ear pain, and cervical lymphadenopathy.

Tonsillar carcinoma.description: A cancer of the tonsil that often causes persistent unilateral throat discomfort, referred otalgia, and regional neck node enlargement.

Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma wi.normalized_text: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma with cervical lymph node metastasis
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma wi.description: A squamous cell cancer originating in the upper aerodigestive tract that spreads to cervical lymph nodes, producing a persistent neck mass and throat/ear symptoms.

Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.description: A malignant lymphoid disorder that can present with a painless enlarged cervical lymph node or neck mass, sometimes with nonspecific upper aerodigestive symptoms if adjacent structures are involved.

case: 72-year-old white woman with 10-year history of recurrent cystitis. No systemic symptoms. Physical exam showed slight anemia. Urine cultures were positive for Escherichia coli. No hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy detected by CT and ultrasound. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy and subsequent biopsies were negative for both pathologic lymphoid infiltrate and Helicobacter pylori. Otolaryngologic examination and bone marrow biopsy were negative. Serology for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus was negative. No monoclonal component found in serum protein electrophoresis.

Recurrent uncomplicated bacterial cystit.description: Repeated lower urinary tract infections, commonly caused by Escherichia coli, especially in older women due to postmenopausal urinary changes and other local risk factors.

Chronic lymphocytic leukemia / small lym.normalized_text: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma
Chronic lymphocytic leukemia / small lym.description: A slow-growing lymphoproliferative disorder that can present with anemia and recurrent infections due to immune dysfunction, sometimes with minimal early symptoms.

Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID).description: An immune deficiency characterized by poor antibody production, leading to recurrent bacterial infections and sometimes autoimmune or hematologic abnormalities.

Occult mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue.description: An indolent extranodal B-cell lymphoma that can involve mucosal sites and may be associated with chronic antigenic stimulation or infection.

case: 95-year-old woman admitted after a fall. Medical history includes Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (on metformin). Laboratory findings showed elevated white cell count and C reactive protein levels. Urine culture revealed Klebsiella pneumoniae infection. Blood cultures were negative.

Complicated urinary tract infection (UTI.description: A bacterial infection of the urinary tract occurring in a patient with risk factors such as advanced age, diabetes, and frailty; often associated with inflammatory marker elevation.

Acute pyelonephritis.description: A kidney infection that is usually due to ascending urinary infection and can cause systemic inflammation and marked laboratory abnormalities.

Urosepsis.description: A severe systemic response to a urinary tract infection that may lead to sepsis, often suspected when inflammatory markers are elevated in an infected older adult.

Asymptomatic bacteriuria.description: Presence of bacteria in the urine without classic urinary symptoms; common in older adults, though inflammatory markers may suggest an associated infection rather than simple colonization.

case: 22-year-old athletic male presented with swelling and locking of the left knee. He had no recent trauma but had several football injuries as a child. Two years prior, he had experienced disabling knee pain.

Meniscal tear.description: A tear in the knee meniscus, often caused by twisting injury or repetitive sports-related stress, can lead to pain, swelling, catching, and locking of the knee.

Osteochondritis dissecans.description: A condition in which a segment of bone and overlying cartilage loses blood supply and may loosen, causing knee pain, swelling, and mechanical symptoms such as locking.

Loose body in the knee joint.normalized_text: Loose body in the knee joint
Loose body in the knee joint.description: A free fragment of cartilage or bone within the joint can intermittently block motion and cause swelling, catching, or locking.

Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.normalized_text: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury with secondary meniscal damage
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.description: An ACL injury, often sports-related, can lead to chronic knee instability and associated meniscal damage, producing swelling and mechanical symptoms.

case: 48-year-old male presented with 1-week history of jaundice, dark brown urine, pale stools, and nausea. Medical history and physical exam were unremarkable. Laboratory findings showed hepatic panel in cholestatic pattern: total bilirubin 117 μmol/L, conjugated bilirubin 66.8 μmol/L, alkaline phosphatase 173 IU/L, γ-Glutamyltransferase 380 IU/L, Alanine transaminase 468 IU/L. CA19-9 was 11783 IU/mL. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and β2-microglobulin were normal.

diagnoses.name: Primary pancreatic T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.normalized_text: Primary pancreatic T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma

Extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.description: A malignant tumor arising from the bile ducts, often causing obstructive cholestasis and jaundice. CA19-9 can be markedly elevated in this cancer.

Pancreatic adenocarcinoma with biliary o.description: A pancreatic cancer, especially in the head of the pancreas, can compress the common bile duct and cause obstructive jaundice with elevated CA19-9.

Choledocholithiasis.description: Gallstones in the common bile duct can obstruct bile flow, producing jaundice, pale stools, dark urine, and a cholestatic enzyme pattern.

Benign biliary stricture.description: A noncancerous narrowing of the bile ducts can lead to obstructive jaundice and cholestatic liver enzyme abnormalities.

IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis.description: An inflammatory fibro-sclerosing disease of the bile ducts that can mimic cholangiocarcinoma and cause obstructive jaundice with cholestatic labs.

case: 80-year-old woman with 6-month history of slowly increasing asymptomatic lumbar subcutaneous mass. History of chronic renal failure requiring dialysis three times weekly for 10 years. Poor compliance with phosphate-binding medications and dietary restrictions. Physical exam showed firm, immobile subcutaneous nodule measuring 9 cm in major axis. Laboratory findings: serum calcium 1.95 mmol/L (normal: 2.05-2.55), serum phosphorus 3.3 mmol/L (normal: 0.74-1.52), serum intact parathyroid hormone 142 ng/L (normal: 10-65), serum creatinine 787 μmol/L (normal: 53-106).

Uremic tumoral calcinosis.description: A calcium-phosphate crystal deposition disorder seen in patients with chronic kidney disease, often associated with hyperphosphatemia and secondary hyperparathyroidism, causing large periarticular or subcutaneous calcified masses.

Secondary hyperparathyroidism due to chr.normalized_text: Secondary hyperparathyroidism due to chronic kidney disease
Secondary hyperparathyroidism due to chr.description: A compensatory increase in parathyroid hormone caused by chronic hypocalcemia, phosphate retention, and vitamin D abnormalities in advanced kidney disease.

Calcinosis cutis.description: Deposition of insoluble calcium salts in the skin or subcutaneous tissue, which can occur secondary to metabolic abnormalities such as renal failure with calcium-phosphate imbalance.

Hyperphosphatemic familial tumoral calci.description: A rare inherited disorder of phosphate regulation leading to marked hyperphosphatemia and calcium-phosphate deposition in soft tissues.

Soft tissue calcification secondary to e.normalized_text: Soft tissue calcification secondary to end-stage renal disease mineral bone disorder
Soft tissue calcification secondary to e.description: Metastatic calcification in soft tissues caused by disordered calcium-phosphate metabolism in advanced chronic kidney disease.

case: 47-year-old female presented to emergency department after being hit while skiing by another skier at high speed from behind. Immediate pain and marked general swelling of the knee joint occurred after impact. Unable to bear weight. Physical exam showed neurovascularly intact limb with no broken skin. No relevant medical, family, or social history.

Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear.description: A ligament injury in the knee often caused by twisting, deceleration, or direct trauma, leading to pain, swelling, and instability.

Tibial plateau fracture.description: A fracture of the upper part of the tibia at the knee joint, often due to high-energy trauma and associated with rapid swelling and inability to bear weight.

Knee dislocation.description: A severe injury where the tibia and femur lose normal alignment; it can threaten blood vessels and nerves and usually causes major pain and swelling.

Meniscal tear.description: Injury to the knee cartilage that commonly causes pain, swelling, and difficulty bearing weight, often after rotation or trauma.

Patellar dislocation.description: Displacement of the kneecap from its normal position, usually causing sudden pain, swelling, and inability to continue weight-bearing.

case: A 52-year-old woman presented with complaints of anal pain, constipation, and tenesmus for 3 months before being referred to the hospital. There were no relevant prior illnesses. Rectal digital examination revealed a 6-cm smooth elastic mass on the rectal posterior left side 2 cm from the anal verge. Colonoscopy showed a rectal submucosal bulging. Computed tomography scan and magnetic resonance imaging confirmed the presence of a single 6-cm well-delimited mass, compressing and infiltrating the wall of the medium to low rectum.

diagnoses.name: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
diagnoses.icd11_title: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour of unspecified gastrointestinal sites

Rectal gastrointestinal stromal tumor (G.description: A mesenchymal tumor arising from the interstitial cells of Cajal in the gastrointestinal tract; in the rectum it often presents as a well-circumscribed submucosal mass and may cause compressive symptoms.

Rectal leiomyoma.description: A benign smooth muscle tumor that can arise in the rectum and appear as a well-defined submucosal lesion, sometimes causing local pressure symptoms.

Rectal schwannoma.description: A rare benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor that can present as a submucosal rectal mass and is typically well circumscribed on imaging.

Rectal lipoma.description: A benign tumor of adipose tissue in the rectum; larger lesions can cause obstructive or pressure-related symptoms and may appear as a smooth submucosal mass.

case: Two-year-four-month-old female with intrauterine growth restriction at birth (39 weeks, C-section; birth weight 1850 g, length 44.5 cm, head circumference 31 cm, all 3rd percentile). At 3 months, evaluation for suspected hearing loss showed bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss on ABR, and hearing aids were placed at 4 months. During infancy, she had persistent poor growth with weight and height below the 3rd percentile, but normal psychomotor development (sat at 8 months, walked at 14 months, talked at 13 months). CNS MRI was normal. Genetic testing identified a novel de novo heterozygous PIK3R1 variant c.1956dupT (p.Lys653*) in exon 15.

SHORT syndrome.description: A rare genetic disorder caused most often by pathogenic variants in PIK3R1, characterized by short stature, characteristic facial features, delayed dentition, eye and dental abnormalities, insulin resistance/lipoatrophy, and prenatal or postnatal growth restriction.

PIK3R1-related growth disorder / PIK3R1-.normalized_text: PIK3R1-related growth disorder / PIK3R1-associated syndromic short stature
PIK3R1-related growth disorder / PIK3R1-.description: A broader category of disorders caused by pathogenic PIK3R1 variants that can present with prenatal growth retardation, postnatal growth failure, and variable multisystem involvement, sometimes overlapping with SHORT syndrome.

Congenital sensorineural hearing loss.description: Hearing loss present at birth or detected early in infancy, often due to genetic causes, with normal or near-normal neurologic development depending on the underlying etiology.

Primordial dwarfism / severe intrauterin.normalized_text: Primordial dwarfism / severe intrauterine and postnatal growth retardation syndrome
Primordial dwarfism / severe intrauterin.description: A group of rare conditions characterized by marked growth restriction beginning before birth and continuing after birth, often with proportionate short stature and variable developmental or congenital anomalies.

Tybjerg syndrome / syndromic growth fail.normalized_text: Tybjerg syndrome / syndromic growth failure due to PI3K-AKT pathway dysregulation
Tybjerg syndrome / syndromic growth fail.description: A conceptual differential for disorders involving the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway that may cause growth abnormalities and other developmental features, though the exact phenotype can vary widely depending on the gene involved.
